data.title: When the fan stopped
data.goal: Describe what changes in a room and explain why you still choose to stay.

data.situation: On Friday evening, Lin came home along the path through the park. She put the notebook from her three morning journeys on the small table beside the door. Jo had lent her a fan for the warm afternoons. It stood at the other end of the table, turning from side to side. A low rattle filled the room. Lin looked towards the window, then noticed a sheet of paper trembling beside the fan. When Jo arrived, Lin switched the fan off. There was a noticeable difference: the rattle stopped, and they no longer had to raise their voices. Footsteps from the flat above were still audible. Lin switched the fan on once more; the rattle returned. She wrote down what she had heard, without blaming the window or the neighbours. Jo offered to take the fan home and look at it. With the fan out of the way, Lin moved the notebook onto the desk by the window. The replacement screw had arrived earlier that week, and the desk could finally stand firmly. She opened the window a little. The room was quiet enough for her to read the page, although an occasional car passed outside. The lamp was still on the small table by the door; its light barely reached the desk. The flat had not grown any bigger, and Lin still had to choose where each piece of furniture would go. Nevertheless, she was glad she had chosen it. The walk to work was manageable, and she now had a quiet place to sit in the evening. She left the notebook open on the desk. Tomorrow, she and Jo would move the little table and bring the lamp closer.
data.easySummary: Lin returns from work and hears a rattle. Switching off the fan makes a noticeable difference. The flat is still small. Nevertheless, she likes the short walk and the quiet desk. She plans to move the lamp closer.
data.easySummaryZh: 林下班回家，听见咔嗒声。关掉风扇后，声音明显不同。公寓仍然小，但她喜欢方便的步行路程和安静的书桌。她准备把台灯挪近一点。

retrievalPrompts.cue: The rattle stops when Lin turns the fan off. Tell Jo what changed.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 风扇关掉后，咔嗒声停了。告诉乔，你察觉到了什么变化。
acceptableAnswers: There was a noticeable difference when the fan stopped. The rattle disappeared.
retrievalPrompts.feedback: Name the change you could actually hear.
checks: 变化限定为风扇声，不说楼上脚步声也消失

retrievalPrompts.cue: The flat is small, but the walk to work and the quiet desk suit Lin. Explain why she is still glad she chose it.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 公寓小，但步行上班和安静的书桌符合林的需要。说明为什么她仍高兴选了这里。
acceptableAnswers: The flat is small. Nevertheless, Lin is glad she chose it because the walk and the desk suit her.
retrievalPrompts.feedback: Keep both the drawback and the reason for staying.
retrievalPrompts.feedbackZh: 既说出缺点，也说明住下的理由。
checks: 用nevertheless连接仍愿意住下的判断

retrievalPrompts.cue: Lin can hear Jo more easily now, although the flat above is not silent. Explain the difference without claiming that every sound is gone.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 林现在更容易听清乔说话，但楼上并非一点声音也没有。说明区别，不说所有声音都消失了。
acceptableAnswers: There is a noticeable difference without the fan. Nevertheless, we can still hear footsteps from upstairs.
retrievalPrompts.feedback: The footsteps are a limit to the change, not proof that nothing improved.
retrievalPrompts.feedbackZh: 脚步声说明变化的限度，不代表完全没有改善。
checks: 有可察觉的风扇声变化

transferPrompt.cue: You move away from a noisy printer and can hear yourself think. The new seat is farther from the books you need, but you prefer it for writing. Tell a friend what changed and why you will stay there.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 你从吵闹的打印机旁挪开，思路清楚了。新座位离需要的书更远，但你更愿意在那里写作。告诉朋友变化，以及留下的理由。
acceptableAnswers: There is a noticeable difference away from the printer. The books are farther away. Nevertheless, I prefer this seat for writing.
transferPrompt.feedback: Use the library facts; a room or a fan is no longer involved.
transferPrompt.feedbackZh: 依据图书馆的新情况表达，不再套用房间和风扇。
